sweep_summary: Lamang (lama1288) is not in the catalog. All three works with stress in the title are Wolff's papers on Firthian palatalisation/labialisation 'prosodies' in Lamang-Hdi (2004 WOCAL4 pp. 43-65, two duplicate Glottolog records; 2006 Topics in Chadic Linguistics II pp. 141-154): prosody-but-not-word-stress, print-only Koeppe volumes, no open copy; the only stress-related snippet from the 2004 paper is a remark that stress/tone/pitch accent are unresolved for Proto-Chadic. Priority low. The real stress statement for Lamang is Wolff 1983 Grammar secs. 6.2-6.3, recovered here from Google Books snippet view (feeds endpoint works from the box; search-inside pages and HathiTrust are blocked): a non-distinctive optional accent on the penultimate syllable (higher pitch and/or lengthening, skipped when the penult is schwa; first-syllable accent in words with a syllabic-sonorant onset) plus purely morphophonological, never lexical 'stress' marking plural verbal nouns, associative constructions and focus forms, in an otherwise tonal language. Wolff 2015 vol. 1 (secs. 2.2.2.3 'Non-contrastive accent and downdrift' p. 88, 2.2.2.4 'Morphophonologically induced stress' p. 91, 3.3 p. 367ff) is the fullest modern statement but is print-only (high priority to acquire, with the 1983 grammar); Wolff 1988 'Ablaut and accent in Chadic' (De Gruyter, paywalled) and Wolff 2013 (Peeters, snippet: 'pitch accent and (contrastive) stress accent play some role') are medium. Everything downloaded is under ( appended; consolidated verbatim snippets). all lookups used automated download/direct download on Glottolog, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Google Books feeds, Koeppe, Peeters and De Gruyter.

new_statements.quote: Accent is characterized by prominence (higher pitch and/or longer duration of the vowel; cf. "stress" 6.3.) of the penultimate syllable, unless its vowel is schwa [...] In case of schwa in the penultimate syllable, prominence is shifted according to certain low level rules [...] 6.3. Stress [...] The functional load of stress (marked on vowels in phonological representation) is relatively low in Lamang. It has been found to be a concomitant feature of (a) plural verbal noun formation, (b) regular associative constructions, and (c) focus [...] Stress never has lexical function in the language, its occurrence is of purely morphophonological nature, i.e., it always accompanies a morpheme which can be identified on independent grounds.

new_statements.reading: Lamang is a tone language (Wolff: a 'split system' of lexical/grammatical tone and phonetic pitch). It has no lexical word stress. There is a non-distinctive, optional phonetic 'accent' = prominence (higher pitch and/or lengthening) on the PENULTIMATE syllable in pre-pausal/citation forms, skipping a schwa penult (prominence then shifts, examples show antepenultimate), and falling on the first syllable in words that begin with a syllabic sonorant. 'Stress' proper is purely morphophonological: it marks plural verbal nouns, associative constructions (on the final syllable of the head noun before linker -a) and focus forms. For a word-stress catalog: no phonological stress; non-contrastive penultimate accent (schwa-skipping); morphological stress only.
